fields.description: Stable, unique ID that never changes when the geometry is edited. Vermont districts use VTFD-0001; service areas may use the PWSID.
service_area or political_district. See §8.
Official name, e.g. *Danville Fire District 1*. For water systems, use the name as registered in SDWIS.
Two-letter postal code.
Town(s) the boundary falls in, separated by semicolons.
County or counties, separated by semicolons.

fields.level: Required for service areas; Recommended for districts
fields.description: Public Water System ID: two letters plus seven digits, e.g. VT0005037. A district that runs several systems lists them all, separated by semicolons. One district is **not** always one system.
Active, Inactive, Dissolved, Merged.
Area computed in an equal-area or state-plane CRS, not in degrees.
Anything a user should know that fits nowhere else.
Entity that created the boundary, e.g. *Danville Fire District*, *RCAP Solutions*, *VT ANR*.
Type of that entity.
How the geometry was produced: GIS data, heads-up digitization, manual digitization, modeled, other.
What it was produced from: a plat, a legal description, parcels, a town boundary, water lines, and so on.
Plain-language account of the steps, e.g. *"Traced from 1962 plat, Book 40 p. 112, georeferenced to VCGI parcels."*
The specific source used: map title, plat book and page, survey name, file name.
Link to the source document or dataset.
Date of the **source material**, e.g. when the plat was drawn. This is often decades before the GIS file.
Date the GIS boundary was first created.
Date the geometry or attributes last changed.
Who distributes the dataset, if different from the provider.
Person and organization who sent the file.
Date it was received.
CRS of the file as received, e.g. EPSG:5646.
Y if no CRS was declared and it had to be worked out.
Verified, Not Verified, Pending, Unknown.
Date it was verified; blank if not verified.
How it was verified, e.g. *"Prudential committee reviewed printed map against district records."*
Type of entity that verified it.
Person and role, e.g. *"Jane Doe, district clerk."* (California records this.)
Planned re-check, e.g. *"After each annexation"*, *"Every 5 years"*.
Estimated horizontal accuracy in meters; -1 means unknown. (Adapted from Oregon's admin-boundary standard.)
Scale denominator of a paper source, e.g. 24000. (From Missouri.)
Fire District, Water District, Consolidated Water District, Other Special District.
Water, Wastewater, Water & Wastewater, Fire, Other, separated by semicolons.
What legally establishes the boundary: legislative charter, municipal vote/order, ordinance, resolution, court order, other, unknown.
Citation for that authority, e.g. 24 V.S.A. App. ch. 505, § 2, or *"Town of Danville selectboard order, 1948"*. Write unknown if none has been found.
**Verbatim** boundary language from the authority, if any, e.g. *"The corporate limits shall be the boundary lines of the Town of Williamstown…"*
Land-records reference for a recorded plat or description, e.g. *"Book 111, page 184, Town of Wilmington land records."*
Relation to the town: coextensive_with_town, sub_town, multi_town, approximate.
Date the district was legally formed. (Colorado and TCEQ record this.)
Date the **current** boundary took legal effect: the formation date, or the date of the most recent annexation. Not the GIS edit date. (Oregon's standard is explicit on this.)
Earlier names, separated by semicolons. (From Colorado.)
E.g. *Prudential Committee*, *Board of Water Commissioners*.
The district's own site.
Census of Governments ID, if the district appears there.
Area stated in the legal record, if any. Compare with area_sqkm; a large gap signals a digitizing problem. (TCEQ and Ventura LAFCo record both.)
